This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging the judgment dated 13.07.2023 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Member MACT V, Vijayapura in MVC No.203/2021.
Janamunnissa vs Pappu Ram Dewasi And Anr on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33638510/

sentences.text:
Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 22.11.2020 at about 5.45 p.m.,
near Managuli Ring Road, NH-52, Vijayapura, the claimant along with her son was proceeding from Katnalli to her native Babanagar Village on a motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-33/U-6844 as a pillion rider.
Her son was riding the said motorcycle on the extreme left side of the road.

At that time, the driver of the lorry bearing Registration no.RJ-19/GB-6584 came from the opposite direction from Almatti towards Solapur, at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, and abruptly came towards the motorcycle and dashed to it.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that she spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded NC: 2025:KHC-K:6583-DB HC-KAR that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.7,98,700/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
The respondent no.2 shall indemnify the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation NC: 2025:KHC-K:6583-DB HC-KAR amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

6. Sri. Sanganabasava, learned counsel appearing for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimant examined the doctor as PW.2.
In his evidence, he deposed that the claimant had suffered 26% disability to the left lower limb.
The Tribunal has assessed the whole-body disability as 8% which is on the lower side.
b) Secondly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
She was treated as inpatient for a period of 91 days.
She has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering the same, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal for Pain and Suffering, loss of amenities and other incidental expenses is on the lower side.
Hence, sought for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, Smt. Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter-contentions:
a) Firstly, due to the accident, the injuries suffered by the claimant are minor in nature.
She has examined the Doctor.
Doctor has deposed that claimant has suffered 26% disability to left lower limb.
Considering the evidence of doctor and medical records, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the whole body disability as 8%.
b) Secondly, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant, medical records and evidence of doctor, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.

It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 22.11.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle NC: 2025:KHC-K:6583-DB HC-KAR by its driver of the lorry bearing registration No.RJ-19/GB- 6584.
10.
As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained fracture of lower one third of left femur and tibia and lacerated wound over nose bridge.
She has examined the doctor as PW.2.

In his evidence,
he has deposed that the claimant has suffered permanent impairment in relation to the left lower limb to the extent of 26%.

Considering the evidence of doctor and wound certificate-Ex.P5,
discharge summary-Ex.P6 and disability certificate-Ex.P11, we are of the opinion that whole body disability has to be assessed to 10%.
The Tribunal has rightly considered the monthly income of the claimant as Rs.13,750/- and rightly taken the multiplier applicable to her age group as '13'.
Thus, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,14,500/- (Rs.13,750*12*13*10%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
11. Due to the accident claimant has suffered grievous injuries.
She was inpatient for a period of 91 days.
She NC: 2025:KHC-K:6583-DB HC-KAR has suffered lot of pain during the treatment.
She has to suffer this disability and unhappiness throughout her life.

Considering the evidence of doctor and injuries suffered by the claimant, we are inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Pain and Suffering' from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.60,000/-and under the head of 'loss of amenities' from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
12.
Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

13. Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:

Accordingly, we pass the following order:

ii) The judgment and award of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
